governing: bolts (bolt shear, eccentric bolt group by the instantaneous-center method)
notes: ASD, AISC 360-22. Ten 3/4 in Group 120 (A325-N) bolts, snug-tight in standard holes, 2 columns x 5 rows, 3 in pitch, 5-1/2 in gauge (the W12x40 workable gauge; 1.255 in edge to the flange tips), 1-1/4 in vertical and horizontal plate edges, PL 3/8 x 14-1/2 A572 Gr 50. Bolt group: IC coefficient C = 4.61 for e = 8 in, so Rn/Omega = 4.61 x 23.9/2.00 = 55.0 kip against 39.9 kip (0.73); the elastic method gives 0.88. Per-bolt bearing and tearout (J3.11a, deformation considered, shortest clear distance taken in every direction) are 24.7 kip on the plate and 34.1 kip on the column flange, both above the 23.9 kip bolt shear, so bolt shear governs. Plate at the outer bolt column with M = V(e - g/2) = 209 kip-in: flexural yield 0.42, flexural rupture on the net section 0.47, buckling (Part 9 double-cope method) 0.53. Taking the full M = V e = 319 kip-in as a conservative bound: rupture 0.72, F11 lateral-torsional yield 0.72, buckling with Fcr S 0.82. Shear yield 0.37, shear rupture 0.54, block shear 0.51. Spacing and edge distances meet J3.3, J3.4 and J3.5. The plate has to extend past the load line (8 in from the bolt centroid, about 4 in beyond the flange tip), with the load delivered there. Outside the connection's scope: the column has to be checked for the weak-axis moment V e = 319 kip-in that the bracket puts into it.
